results.name: SOCKS4 + HTTPS proxy live (WP-14): https://pypi.org/ through pproxy's SOCKS4 server (it logs an IPv4 address — the NAME never reached the proxy, it was resolved here through the guard) and through pproxy as an HTTPS proxy (TLS to the proxy verified against a CA in NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, pypi.org named only inside that TLS); without that CA the proxy is refused at TLS and never learns the destination

PAC failover live (WP-14): "PROXY <dead>; SOCKS <pproxy>; DIRECT" — pypi.org is carried by the SECOND entry (SOCKS = v4, Chrome's reading), the failover is recorded, and a repeat request goes straight to the healthy proxy (the dead one is remembered for 5 min, no second failover); a POST of 70 KB of mixed UTF-8 / binary-safe text fails over byte-exact (echo site's SHA-256) and the dead proxy received only the proxy handshake, never a byte of the body; a proxy that ANSWERS 403 for the destination is not failed over — no DIRECT leak

KDE live (WP-15): a fresh process in a KDE session (XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=KDE), with no proxy variables and no gsettings, reads ~/.config/kioslaverc (here via XDG_CONFIG_HOME) written in KDE 5's "http://host port" form and sends https://pypi.org/ through the proxy it names (pproxy logs it); ProxyType=0 means direct

WPAD live (WP-15): the machine's REAL resolver — "search eng.corp.fusion-test.example" in /etc/resolv.conf, wpad.corp.fusion-test.example in /etc/hosts, the PAC file on port 80 — GNOME "auto" with an empty URL (stand-in gsettings) and KDE ProxyType=3 each DISCOVER it by devolution (wpad → wpad.eng.… fail, wpad.corp.… answers; wpad.fusion-test.example is never needed) and pypi.org goes through the SOCKS proxy it names; with nothing to discover, auto-detect falls back to DIRECT with the tried list reported
